e-8883.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Sphere Using Spherical Coordinates
e-8883.problem:
$$
\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi) = \big\langle 5 \cos\theta\sin\phi, \: \text{_____}, \: 5 \cos\phi \big\rangle
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as $x^2+y^2+z^2=25.$ What is the second component of $\mathbf{f}?$
e-8883.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =5.$

If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad
y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 
z = \rho\cos\phi.
$$

 

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi)$ and $\phi \in [-\pi,\pi].$

Therefore, the second component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{black} 5 \sin\theta\sin\phi}.$

e-8882.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of an Ellipsoid Using Spherical Coordinates
e-8882.problem:
$$
\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi) = \big\langle \text{_____} , \:  5\sin\theta\sin\phi, \: 4\cos\phi\big\rangle
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi)$ above parametrizes the ellipsoid defined in Cartesian coordinates as 

$$
\dfrac{x^2}{36}+\dfrac{y^2}{25}+\dfrac{z^2}{16}=1.
$$

What is the first component of $\mathbf{f}?$
e-8882.worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x = 6X, \qquad
y =5 Y, \qquad
z = 4Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our ellipsoid, we get

$$
X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = 1,
$$

which is the equation of a sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =1.$

If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad
Y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 
Z = \rho\cos\phi.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨6X,5Y,4Z⟩ \\  & =⟨6\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨6\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi)$ and $\phi \in [-\pi,\pi].$

Therefore, the first component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{black}6\cos\theta\sin\phi}.$

e-8884.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Cone Using Cylindrical Coordinates
e-8884.problem:
$$
\mathbf{f}(r,\theta) = \big\langle \text{_____}, \: 6r\sin\theta, \: r \big\rangle, \qquad r \geq 0
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(r,\theta)$ above parametrizes the half-cone defined in Cartesian coordinates as 

$$
z^2=\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{36}, \qquad z\geq 0.
$$

 

What is the first component of $\mathbf{f}?$
e-8884.worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x = 5X, \qquad
y = 6Y, \qquad
z = Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our half-cone, we get

$$
Z^2=X^2+Y^2,\qquad Z\geq 0
$$

which is the equation of a half-cone whose axis of symmetry is the $Z$-axis in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates. In cylindrical polar coordinates, this cone has the equation $Z = r.$

If $(r, \theta, Z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X = r\cos\theta, \qquad
Y = r\sin\theta, \qquad 
Z = Z.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨5X,\,6Y\,,\,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨5\cdot r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,6\cdot r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨5r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,6r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r \in [0,\infty)$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi).$

Therefore, the first component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{black} 5r\cos\theta}.$

content.problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨\text{_____},\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2.$ What is the first component of $f?$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =\sqrt{2}.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

content.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $7$ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =7.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨7\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$ 

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $7\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨_____,3sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,3cos⁡ϕ⟩

The vector-valued function f(θ,ϕ) above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as x2+y2+z2=3. What is the first component of f?

a
3cos⁡θsin⁡θ
b
3cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ
c
3cos⁡θcos⁡ϕ
d
3sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ
e
3sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given equation generates a sphere of radius 3 centered at the origin. In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation ρ=3.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found using the following formulas: x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following:

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨3⋅cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,3⋅sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,3⋅cos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨3cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,3sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,3cos⁡ϕ⟩

where θ∈[0,2π) and ϕ∈[−π,π].

Therefore, the first component of f is 3cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Sphere Using Spherical Coordinates
content.problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨\text{_____},\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=3.$ What is the first component of $f?$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =\sqrt{3}.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{3}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

The vector-valued function f(θ,ϕ) above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as x2+y2+z2=25. What is the third component of f?

5cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ
b
5sin⁡θ
c
5cos⁡ϕ
d
5sin⁡θcos⁡ϕ
e
25sin⁡ϕ

EXPLANATION

The given equation generates a sphere of radius 5 centered at the origin. In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation ρ=5.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found using the following formulas: x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following:

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨5⋅cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,5⋅sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,5⋅cos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨5cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,5sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,5cos⁡ϕ⟩

where θ∈[0,2π) and ϕ∈[−π,π].

Therefore, the third component of f is 5cos⁡ϕ.

content.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =5.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $5\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨_____,πsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,πcos⁡ϕ⟩

The vector-valued function f(θ,ϕ) above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as x2+y2+z2=π2. What is the first component of f?

a
πcos⁡ϕsin⁡θ
b
πsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ
c
ϕcos⁡θsin⁡π
d
πcos⁡θcos⁡ϕ
e
πcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ
Submit

EXPLANATION

The given equation generates a sphere of radius π centered at the origin. In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation ρ=π.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found using the following formulas: x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following:

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨π⋅cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,π⋅sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,π⋅cos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨πcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,πsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,πcos⁡ϕ⟩

where θ∈[0,2π) and ϕ∈[−π,π].

Therefore, the first component of f is πcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Sphere Using Spherical Coordinates
content.problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨\text{_____},\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}={\pi }^{2}.$ What is the first component of $f?$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $\pi $ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =\pi .$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

after.problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\text{_____},\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the ellipsoid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{{x}^{2}}{36}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=1.$ What is the second component of $f?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x=6X,\,y=3Y,\,z=4Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our ellipsoid, we get

$$
{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}+{Z}^{2}=1,
$$

which is the equation of a sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =1.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨6X,3Y,4Z⟩ \\  & =⟨6\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,3\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨6\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,3\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

$$

$$

$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨6X,3Y,4Z⟩ \\  & =⟨6\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,3\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨6\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,3\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

$$

content.worked_solution:

$$

$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our ellipsoid, we get

$$

$$
X=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$

$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

content.worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x=3X,\,y=2Y,\,z=\frac{1}{5}Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our ellipsoid, we get

$$
{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}+{Z}^{2}=1,
$$

which is the equation of a sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =1.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨3X,2Y,\frac{1}{5}Z⟩ \\  & =⟨3\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,2\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{1}{5}\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨3\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,2\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{1}{5}\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

after.worked_solution:

$$

$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our half-cone, we get

$$

$$

If $(r,\theta ,Z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=Z.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2X,Y,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

The vector-valued function f(r,θ) above parametrizes the half-cone defined in Cartesian coordinates as z2=x24+y2 for z≥0. What is the first component of f?

b
12rcos⁡θ
c
2rcos⁡θ

14rsin⁡θ

4rcos⁡θ

EXPLANATION

First, we make the following substitution:

x=2X,y=Y,z=Z

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our half-cone, we get

Z2=X2+Y2,Z≥0

which is the equation of a half-cone whose axis of symmetry is the Z-axis in (X,Y,Z) coordinates. In cylindrical polar coordinates, this cone has the equation Z=r.

If (r,θ,Z) are the cylindrical coordinates of a point, then its (X,Y,Z) coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

X=rcos⁡θ,Y=rsin⁡θ,Z=Z.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following:

f(r,θ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨2X,Y,Z⟩=⟨2rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,Z⟩=⟨2rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,r⟩

where r∈[0,∞) and θ∈[0,2π).

Therefore, the first component of f is 2rcos⁡θ.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Cone Using Cylindrical Coordinates
content.problem:
$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨\text{_____},\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩,\,r\ge 0
$$

The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta )$ above parametrizes the half-cone defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${z}^{2}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{y}^{2}$ for $z\ge 0.$ What is the first component of $f?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x=2X,\,y=Y,\,z=Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our half-cone, we get

$$
{Z}^{2}={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2},\,Z\ge 0
$$

which is the equation of a half-cone whose axis of symmetry is the $Z$-axis in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates. In cylindrical polar coordinates, this cone has the equation $Z=r.$

If $(r,\theta ,Z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=Z.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2X,Y,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$
